full_judgment:
2. The appellants herein as plaintiffs instituted Other Class Suit No. 322 of 2001 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Sirajgonj, for declaration of title. The plaintiff stated, inter alia, that the suit property measuring an area of 6.30 acres of land belonged to Asutosh Sarker, Jagodish Sarker, Hrishikesh Sarker, Debendra Nath Sarkar and Gangamoyee Sarker. The plaintiffs' predecessor took settlement of the said lands from the said landlords' by several amalnamas and they were recognised as korfa tenants under khatian Nos.22-31 of the landlords' khatian No.21. The lands were accordingly recorded in the C.S. khatian in the names of the plaintiffs' predecessors and they exercised their title and possession over statutory period. Of the said tenants, Adam Pramanik died leaving plaintiff No.1 as daughter and brother plaintiff No.2, who died leaving behind two sons, namely Afer Pramanik and Wafor Pramanik, who also died leaving 3 sons plaintiffs Nos.3-5. Afer Pramanik died leaving 4 sons plaintiffs Nos.6-9. Rabi Pramanik died leaving one daughter plaintiff No.10. Gazi Pramanik died leaving 2 sons, namely Biru Pramanik and Miruddin Pramanik. Biru Pramanik died leaving 2 sons plaintiff Nos.11 and 12. Arajdi Pramanik died leaving son plaintiff No.13 and other plaintiffs have also inherited the suit lands from their predecessors. Plaintiff No.1 also sold some lands to plaintiffs Nos. 21-32 on 9th April, 1979. Defendant Nos. 3-9 gifted .33 acre of land in favour of plaintiff No.47. Plaintiff Nos. 23-29 sold .30 acre of land to plaintiffs Monjur Rahman, Abdul Kader and Mohsin Reza. Some other plaintiffs also sold some lands to other plaintiffs and in this way they have been in possession by way of inheritance and purchase. The defendants have no right title and interest in the suit lands. During the last settlement operation the record was initially prepared in the names of their predecessors. Subsequently, it was detected that the S.A. khatian was prepared in the name of Jagodish Sarker which was incorrect. During the war of liberation, the plaintiffs' documents were destroyed and taking advantage of the situation, defendant No.1 created some ante-dated papers and instituted a suit in the Court of Munsif, Sirajgonj and obtained a fraudulent decree by practicing fraud upon the Court. The plaintiffs are not bound by the said decree. During the R.S. operation the plaintiffs went to record their names, when defendant No.1 protested by producing the said fraudulent decree. Hence, the plaintiffs filed the suit. 

 3. Defendant Nos.2, 5 and 6 filed two separate written statements, but defendant No.2 did not contest the suit. Defendant Nos.5 and 6 who are respondent Nos. l and 2 herein stated, inter alia, that they purchased the suit lands measuring 6.30 acres appertaining to C.S. khatian Nos.22- 31 by two registered deeds dated 30th December, 1976. Their further case is that the suit lands belonged to Jagodish Sarker, Asutosh Sarker, Hrishikesh Sarker, Debendra Nath Sarker, sons of Taroni Chandra Sarker and Gongamoyee Sarker, wife of late Taroni Sarker. While the aforesaid owners were enjoying the said lands by an amicable partition, Jagodish Chandra Sarker got the suit lands but other co-sharers-defendant Nos.2 and 3 got 100 bighas of land under Mouja Porjona. Jagodish Chandra Sarker settled the said lands to the predecessor of the defendants Hossain Ali on 11th Kartick, 1352 B.S. During the S.A. operation, Jagodish Chandra's name was wrongly recorded. Accordingly, Hossain Ali instituted Title Suit No.140 of 1975 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Pabna for declaration of title against Jagodish Chandra Sarker and the suit was decreed ex parte on 29th January, 1974. Pursuant to the decree, Hossain Ali's name was recorded in the S.A. khatian. Subsequently, Hossain Ali instituted Other Class Suit No.282 of 1976 against Assistant Custodian for permanent injunction. During the R.S. operation Jagodish Chandra Sarker's name was recorded, but on appeal the defendant's name was corrected. Defendant No.6 thereupon transferred some lands to Hossain Ali Sarker, Sufia Khatun, Sakera Khatun and others. The plaintiffs have no right, title and interest in the suit land. 

 10. The trial Court observed that the decree in Other Class Suit No.140 of 1974 is not binding of the plaintiffs since they or their predecessor were not party to that suit and similarly in Other Class Suit No.282 of 1976 neither the plaintiffs nor their predecessor were party and hence the decree is not binding upon the plaintiffs. It was further observed that defendant No. 1 having claimed that he took pattan of the suit land, could not produce the original amalnama or dakhila and did not give any satisfactory explanation. As a result the claim of defendant Nos.5/6 regarding the alleged pattan is not believable. However, the trial Court then went on to consider that the mutation khatian and rent receipts are evidence to prove their possession. It is noted that the trial Court took into account the submission of the learned Advocate for the plaintiffs that defendant No.5 who deposed as D.W. I admitted that he was the Nayeb in the Tahsil Office and that the submission of the learned Advocate for the plaintiffs that he had created false and forged pattan and obtained mutation and rent receipts in his name with a view to grab the land, was not without basis. Upon considering the evidence of the witnesses and the materials on record, the trial Court concluded that the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land and although defendant Nos.5/6 produced mutation khatian and rent receipts, there is good reason to suspect that those are collusive. However, the trial Court dismissed the suit of the plaintiffs on the finding that the korfa title of the plaintiffs' predecessor subsisted, but they were unable to produce any evidence to prove such title. 

 13. The appellate Court observed that during the pendency of the appeal, the plaintiffs produced certified copy of C.S. khatian No.21 and the original porcha of the khatian Nos.22-29 and 31 as well as the certified copy of khatian No.30, which were marked as exhibit-4 series and admitted into evidence without objection. 

 17. We also note that sub-khatian Nos.22 to 31 of khatian No.21 record the name of the plaintiffs' predecessor Adam Pramanik as korfa tenant since 1922.
